questions.questionTextEn: The correct increasing order of thermal decomposition temperature of alkaline earth metal carbonates is
questions.explanationEn: Smaller cations with higher charge density ($\text{Be}^{2+} > \text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Ca}^{2+} > \text{Sr}^{2+} > \text{Ba}^{2+}$) polarize the large $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ anion more strongly and yield a more exothermic lattice energy upon forming the small oxide $\text{MO}$. Thus, thermal stability increases down the group: $\text{BeCO}_3 < \text{MgCO}_3 < \text{CaCO}_3 < \text{SrCO}_3 < \text{BaCO}_3$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following diatomic species is diamagnetic according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
questions.explanationEn: $\text{NO}^+$ has $14$ total electrons (isoelectronic with $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{CO}$), so all electrons are paired ($\text{BO} = 3$, diamagnetic). $\text{O}_2^+$ ($15\text{ e}^-$), $\text{O}_2^-$ ($17\text{ e}^-$), and $\text{NO}$ ($15\text{ e}^-$) all have an odd number of electrons and are paramagnetic.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Complete hydrolysis of the interhalogen compound $\text{ClF}_3$ with water produces
questions.explanationEn: Hydrolysis of an interhalogen $XX'_n$ (where $X'$ is the more electronegative halogen) yields the hydrohalic acid $\text{H}X'$ and the oxoacid of the less electronegative halogen $X$ in the same oxidation state ($+n$). For $\text{ClF}_3$ ($\text{Cl}$ is $+3$): $\text{ClF}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{HClO}_2 + 3\text{HF}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct increasing order of normal boiling points of the Group 16 hydrides is
questions.explanationEn: From $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$, boiling point increases with molar mass and London dispersion forces ($\text{H}_2\text{S}: -60\,^\circ\text{C} < \text{H}_2\text{Se}: -41\,^\circ\text{C} < \text{H}_2\text{Te}: -2\,^\circ\text{C}$). Water ($+100\,^\circ\text{C}$) has an anomalously high boiling point due to extensive 3D intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Due to the inert pair effect, the strongest oxidizing agent among the following Group 13 and Group 14 ions in aqueous solution is
questions.explanationEn: Relativistic contraction and poor shielding by intervening $4f$ and $5d$ electrons stabilize the $6s^2$ electron pair in thallium. Consequently, $\text{Tl}^{+}$ is much more stable than $\text{Tl}^{3+}$, making $\text{Tl}^{3+}$ a strong oxidizing agent ($E^\circ(\text{Tl}^{3+}/\text{Tl}^+) = +1.25\text{ V}$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Complete hydrolysis of $\text{XeF}_4$ with water produces a mixture of products including
questions.explanationEn: Complete hydrolysis of $\text{XeF}_4$ is a redox disproportionation reaction: $6\text{XeF}_4 + 12\text{H}_2\text{O} \to 4\text{Xe} + 2\text{XeO}_3 + 24\text{HF} + 3\text{O}_2$. By contrast, complete hydrolysis of $\text{XeF}_6$ is non-redox: $\text{XeF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{XeO}_3 + 6\text{HF}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Wade's rules, the boranes $\text{B}_6\text{H}_6^{2-}$, $\text{B}_5\text{H}_9$, and $\text{B}_4\text{H}_{10}$ are classified, respectively, as
questions.explanationEn: Using Wade's rules for $\text{B}_n\text{H}_m^{q-}$: $\text{B}_6\text{H}_6^{2-}$ ($n=6$, $n+1=7$ SEP) is *closo*; $\text{B}_5\text{H}_9$ ($\text{B}_n\text{H}_{n+4}$, $n=5$, $n+2=7$ SEP) is *nido*; $\text{B}_4\text{H}_{10}$ ($\text{B}_n\text{H}_{n+6}$, $n=4$, $n+3=7$ SEP) is *arachno*.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Applying Bent's rule to difluoromethane ($\text{CH}_2\text{F}_2$), how do the $\angle\text{H}-\text{C}-\text{H}$ and $\angle\text{F}-\text{C}-\text{F}$ bond angles compare to the ideal tetrahedral angle ($109.5^\circ$)?
optionsEn: Both $\angle\text{H}-\text{C}-\text{H}$ and $\angle\text{F}-\text{C}-\text{F}$ are strictly equal to $109.5^\circ$
questions.explanationEn: By Bent's rule, carbon directs hybrids with greater $p$-character toward the more electronegative $\text{F}$ atoms and greater $s$-character toward the less electronegative $\text{H}$ atoms. Higher $p$-character narrows the angle ($\angle\text{F}-\text{C}-\text{F} \approx 108.3^\circ < 109.5^\circ$) while higher $s$-character widens it ($\angle\text{H}-\text{C}-\text{H} \approx 113.7^\circ > 109.5^\circ$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Silver fluoride ($\text{AgF}$) is readily soluble in water whereas $\text{AgCl}$, $\text{AgBr}$, and $\text{AgI}$ are sparingly soluble. The primary reason is that
optionsEn: $\text{AgF}$ has a much lower lattice energy than $\text{AgI}$

the very high hydration enthalpy of the small $\text{F}^-$ ion outweighs the lattice energy of $\text{AgF}$, whereas $\text{AgCl}$, $\text{AgBr}$, and $\text{AgI}$ gain extra covalent stabilization in the solid lattice
$\text{AgF}$ forms a polymeric covalent chain in water
questions.explanationEn: $\text{F}^-$ is small and hard with a very large exothermic hydration enthalpy ($-515\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), which overcomes the purely ionic lattice energy of $\text{AgF}$. For $\text{AgCl}$, $\text{AgBr}$, and $\text{AgI}$, strong soft–soft polarization between $\text{Ag}^+$ ($4d^{10}$) and larger halides adds extra covalent lattice stabilization while halide hydration enthalpy decreases sharply.

In the Kapustinskii equation, $

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Fajan's rules, which of the following comparison(s) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: $\text{SnCl}_4$ is more covalent and has a lower boiling point than $\text{SnCl}_2$.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: $\text{Sn}^{4+}$ has higher charge and smaller radius than $\text{Sn}^{2+}$, giving $\text{SnCl}_4$ high covalent character (liquid at room temperature).
- (B) True: $\text{I}^-$ is larger and far more polarizable than $\text{F}^-$.
- (C) True: $\text{Be}^{2+}$ is much smaller than $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ and has higher polarizing power.
- (D) False: $\text{Hg}^{2+}$ has a $5d^{10}$ pseudo-noble gas core with much higher polarizing power than $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ($[\text{Ar}]$), so $\text{HgCl}_2$ is much more covalent.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding hydrogen bonding is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: *ortho*-Nitrophenol is more steam-volatile than *para*-nitrophenol because *ortho*-nitrophenol forms intramolecular hydrogen bonds.
Ice is less dense than liquid water at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$ because tetrahedral hydrogen bonding creates an open cage-like crystal lattice.
Acetic acid dimerizes in non-polar solvents like benzene through two intermolecular $\text{O}-\text{H}\cdots\text{O}$ hydrogen bonds.
Hydrogen bonding in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ is stronger than in $\text{NH}_3$.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Intramolecular H-bonding in *o*-nitrophenol prevents intermolecular association, lowering its boiling point and increasing steam volatility.
- (B) True: Each $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ in hexagonal ice (Ice Ih) is tetrahedrally H-bonded, leaving open hexagonal channels.
- (C) True: Carboxylic acids form stable 8-membered cyclic dimers via two H-bonds in non-polar solvents.
- (D) False: Sulfur is much larger and less electronegative than nitrogen, so $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ forms negligible H-bonds compared to $\text{NH}_3$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about lattice energy and the Born–Haber cycle is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: The Born–Haber cycle is an application of Hess's law of constant heat summation.
For alkali metal fluorides, the magnitude of lattice energy decreases in the order $\text{LiF} > \text{NaF} > \text{KF} > \text{RbF} > \text{CsF}$.
A large discrepancy between the Born–Haber experimental lattice energy and the Born–Landé theoretical value (with experimental $|U_0|$ significantly larger) indicates substantial covalent character.
Lattice energy increases as the sum of ionic radii ($r_+ + r_-$) increases.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Born–Haber cycle relies on enthalpy being a state function (Hess's law).
- (B) True: Increasing cation radius down Group 1 increases $r_0$ and lowers $|U_0|$.
- (C) True: Extra covalent bonding (e.g., in $\text{AgI}$) makes experimental $|U_0|$ larger than the purely electrostatic Born–Landé prediction.
- (D) False: $|U_0| \propto 1/(r_+ + r_-)$, so it *decreases* as $r_+ + r_-$ increases.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about Ellingham diagrams for metal oxide formation ($\frac{2x}{y}\text{M} + \text{O}_2 \to \frac{2}{y}\text{M}_x\text{O}_y$) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: Most metal oxide lines slope upward because gaseous $\text{O}_2$ is consumed ($\Delta S^\circ < 0$).
An abrupt upward increase in slope occurs at the boiling point of the metal because $\Delta S^\circ$ becomes even more negative upon vaporizing the reactant metal.
The line for $\text{C}(s) + \text{O}_2(g) \to \text{CO}_2(g)$ is nearly horizontal because $\Delta n_g = 0$ and $\Delta S^\circ \approx 0$.
An oxide whose line lies above $\Delta_f G^\circ = 0$ (such as $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ or $\text{HgO}$ at elevated temperatures) decomposes spontaneously upon heating.
questions.explanationEn: All four statements are fundamental thermodynamic properties of Ellingham diagrams: (A) $\Delta S^\circ < 0 \implies$ positive slope; (B) vaporization of metal increases reactant entropy so $\Delta S^\circ$ becomes more negative and slope $-\Delta S^\circ$ becomes steeper; (C) $\Delta n_g = 0$ gives near-zero slope for $\text{C} \to \text{CO}_2$; (D) $\Delta_f G^\circ > 0$ means the reverse thermal decomposition has $\Delta G^\circ < 0$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In an ionic crystal with oxide anions of radius $r_- = 140\text{ pm}$, the minimum radius (in $\text{pm}$) of a cation that can fit into an octahedral void without destabilizing anion–anion contact is _______. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
For an octahedral void, the limiting radius ratio is $r_+/r_- = \sqrt{2} - 1 \approx 0.4142$.
Therefore, $r_+ = 0.4142 \times 140\text{ pm} = 57.99\text{ pm} \approx 58.0\text{ pm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The oxidation state of xenon in sodium perxenate ($\text{Na}_4\text{XeO}_6$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{Na}_4\text{XeO}_6$, $4(+1) + x + 6(-2) = 0 \implies x = +8$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of $sp^3$-hybridized boron atoms in one formula unit of borax, $\text{Na}_2[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]\cdot 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$ anion contains $2$ tetrahedral ($sp^3$) boron atoms and $2$ trigonal planar ($sp^2$) boron atoms.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Slater's rules, the effective nuclear charge ($Z_{\text{eff}}$) experienced by a $3d$ electron in a neutral manganese atom ($Z = 25$, $[\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^2$) is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
For $\text{Mn}$ ($Z = 25$), the Slater grouping is $(1s)^2(2s,2p)^8(3s,3p)^8(3d)^5(4s)^2$.
For a $3d$ electron, $4s$ electrons do not shield ($0$), four other $3d$ electrons contribute $4 \times 0.35 = 1.40$, and the $18$ inner electrons contribute $18 \times 1.00 = 18.00$.
Thus $\sigma = 19.40$ and $Z_{\text{eff}} = 25 - 19.40 = 5.60$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of $\text{B}-\text{O}-\text{B}$ oxygen bridges in the borax anion $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: In $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$, four oxygens are present as terminal $-\text{OH}$ groups and all $5$ remaining oxo atoms act as $\text{B}-\text{O}-\text{B}$ bridges (four around the outer perimeter of the bicyclic core and one central cross-ring bridge).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn:
The experimental dipole moment of gaseous $\text{HF}$ is $1.82\text{ D}$ and the $\text{H}-\text{F}$ bond length is $91.7\text{ pm}$. The percentage ionic character of $\text{HF}$ is _______ $\%$. *(round off to one decimal place)*

[Given: $1\text{ D} = 3.336 \times 10^{-30}\text{ C m}$; $e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$]
questions.explanationEn:
$\mu_{\text{ionic}} = e \cdot d = (1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C})(91.7 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m}) = 1.46903 \times 10^{-29}\text{ C m}$.
$\mu_{\text{obs}} = 1.82 \times 3.336 \times 10^{-30} = 6.07152 \times 10^{-30}\text{ C m}$.
Percentage ionic character $= \frac{6.07152 \times 10^{-30}}{1.46903 \times 10^{-29}} \times 100\% = 41.33\% \approx 41.3\%$.
